python.package: For structured logging of validation results

interface.name: validate_fixtures
interface.description: Main entry point for fixture validation. Accepts consolidated fixtures from Story 3.1, validates all timestamp fields, and returns same fixtures with ValidationResult attached

interface.name: ValidationResult
interface.signature: class ValidationResult(BaseModel): status (enum), reason (str), fixture_valid (bool), odds_status (str), form_status (str), injuries_status (str), h2h_status (str), data_freshness_score (int 0-100), timestamp (datetime)
interface.description: Data model for validation results. Should be serializable for logging and storage. Tracks which data types passed/failed validation

constraint.rule: NEVER use datetime.utcnow() - use datetime.now(timezone.utc) for Python 3.14+ compatibility. All timestamp comparisons must use UTC timezone-aware datetimes
ALWAYS define custom exceptions in exceptions.py. NEVER use bare except clauses. ALWAYS log exceptions with context including url, status, response body where applicable
Fixtures must be today (±24h). Odds must be < 1 hour old (REJECT if stale). Injuries must be < 12 hours old (accept with degradation). Form must be < 24 hours old (accept with degradation)

Non-invasive validation: Add metadata to fixtures without modifying data. Permissive approach: Accept DEGRADATION status, let downstream decide filtering. Observable: All validation reasons logged for debugging
ALWAYS use asyncio.gather for parallel operations. ALWAYS use async context managers. NEVER block event loop with time.sleep() - use asyncio.sleep. ALWAYS handle asyncio.CancelledError explicitly
Validator module should not have circular imports with consolidator.py. Helper functions prefixed with _ (not exported). ValidationResult should be separate from Fixture model

tests.standards: Unit testing framework: pytest. Test fixtures should mock Fixture objects with various timestamp scenarios (fresh, stale, missing, future). Test validation logic for each data type independently, then aggregation logic. Use parametrized tests for multiple scenarios (e.g., odds age 10min, 30min, 90min). All validation edge cases covered: missing timestamps, future dates, timezone issues. Logging assertions to verify correct log levels (INFO for PASS, WARNING for DEGRADATION, ERROR for CRITICAL). Target 85%+ code coverage for validator.py module.

ideas.idea: Test fixture date validation: fresh fixture (today) → PASS, old fixture (1 day old) → PASS, very old (2 days) → CRITICAL, future fixture (1 day future) → PASS, far future (2 days) → CRITICAL, missing fixture_date → CRITICAL
Test odds freshness: fresh odds (10 min old) → PASS, stale odds (90 min old) → DEGRADATION, very stale (5h) → DEGRADATION, missing odds_timestamp → CRITICAL
Test form freshness: fresh (1h old) → PASS, old (20h old) → PASS, very old (48h) → DEGRADATION, missing form_timestamp → DEGRADATION
Test injuries freshness: fresh (1h old) → PASS, old (8h old) → PASS, very old (18h) → DEGRADATION, missing injuries_timestamp → DEGRADATION
Test overall validation aggregation: all data fresh → PASS, odds stale + form fresh → DEGRADATION, fixture date in future → CRITICAL, multiple degradations → DEGRADATION
Test validation summary logging: verify log output format for each status (INFO, WARNING, ERROR), verify fixture summary message format
Test edge cases: timestamp is None → CRITICAL, timestamp in future → CRITICAL, timestamp very old (10 years) → CRITICAL, timezone naive vs aware handling
